title: Step 1 — Upload release demand
description: Select planning month and segment · Upload the release-plan workbook · Parse item codes, quantities and requested timing · Normalize comparison keys while preserving original item-code spelling · Reject ambiguous normalized collisions loudly

title: Step 2 — Apply planning assumptions
description: Rejection gross-up · Wastage allowance · BOM weight · Machine routing · Production rate or fitting cycle/cavity standard · Downtime and machine availability · Every assumption is shown through the resulting plan evidence

title: Step 3 — Optimize machine assignment
description: Route demand only to capable machines · Balance work across available capacity · Use explicit fallback tiers when item-specific rates are unavailable · Keep unroutable and unweighted items outside the schedule · Never invent a route or weight to force completion

title: Step 4 — Build the shift schedule
description: Day and NIGHT shift blocks · One item per 10-hour NIGHT block · Minimum-run blocks for light loads · Weekly fill by machine · Changeovers, excess hours and unfinished demand · Pipe and fitting schedules remain separately traceable

title: Step 5 — Review machine and item results
description: Machine demand versus available capacity · Item-level material kg and required machine hours · Assignment provenance by machine · Coverage gaps: no BOM, no route, locked-out or idle machine · Completion date and unfinished-demand indicators

title: Operator Machine Plan workbook
description: START HERE instructions · One tab per scheduled machine · Day Sheet for supervisor walk-round · Machine Loading for committed block hours · Item Plan, Not Scheduled, Plan Summary and Source Stock · Orange DAY rows and blue NIGHT rows · Whole block hours on every operator-facing tab

title: Customized Run: plan without persistence
description: Choose category and planning month · Upload item codes with Required Quantity, Qty, Production Plan or Stock · Reuse live routing, BOM, rates, rejection, wastage and downtime · Display machine loads, item statuses and shift blocks · Download the operator workbook · Leave no Plan Run, Follow-Up or uploaded-file record

title: Freeze, re-freeze and finalize
description: A pending run retains its uploaded demand · Freeze captures the engine result and schedule lines · Re-freeze regenerates a missing pending result from stored demand · Finalization marks the approved planning state · Frozen lines support later comparison and Follow-Up · Pipe-only and fitting-only runs remain valid scenarios

title: Follow-Up: plan versus actual
description: Join frozen plan lines to actual production by normalized machine and item · Compare plan-to-date with elapsed plan days · Surface quantity, timing, machine and data warnings · Sort warnings by severity · Preserve runs that have actuals even when no plan lines were written · Export follow-up analysis as a specialist workbook

title: Data Verification: does it reconcile?
description: Read-only reconciliation layer · Display computed figures with provenance · Compare independent source paths within tolerance · Record the verification audit trail · Never alter a production fact to make a check pass · Keep verification separate from confirmation gating

title: Manifest, freshness and source health
description: Expected-versus-fetched source coverage · Schema flags for malformed or incomplete layouts · Source-content fingerprints detect change · Last-synced visibility · Cache refresh and shared sheet cache · Honest partial-data banners instead of monthly fallback substitution

title: Reconciliation and precedence rules
description: Daily tabs drive monthly and financial-year headlines · Summary grids are independent reconciliation references · Daily-first totals are never forced down to match an undercounting grid · Sub-monthly windows never borrow monthly values · Units remain plant-specific: kg, litres or pieces · Idle and unparseable sources are different states

title: Source provenance and audit trail
description: Metric → plant → period → workbook → tab · Parse notes explain source-layout decisions · Acknowledgements and sign-offs remain traceable · User activity records safe route-derived labels · Planning runs preserve assumptions and frozen lines · Exports remain reproducible from the same computed facts

title: Failure handling by design
description: Missing future sheets do not become a request storm · Per-source throttling does not erase unrelated data · Empty source templates are reported as idle where appropriate · Ambiguous routing collisions fail loudly · Partial report bundles retain successful files · Time-bounded external calls protect production response times

title: Operating rhythm
description: Daily: review latest meaningful date, exceptions, losses and Day Sheet · Weekly: review machine fill, unfinished demand and Follow-Up warnings · Monthly: reconcile reports, confirm sources and freeze approved plans · Financial-year: review trend, costing and source completeness · On every refresh: preserve provenance and re-gate changed data

title: Metric and unit glossary
description: Output: net or gross production as defined by the source · Rejection: rejected kg or pieces at the correct reporting grain · Efficiency: achieved output against running-time potential · Utilisation: actual run hours against valid ideal-hours capacity · Machine hours: productive requirement · Block hours: operator-committed shift time · Rates: kg/hr for pipe; pcs/hr or cycle/cavity for fittings
